text.en: If a place has many young children, it needs schools. If it has many older people, it needs hospitals. Population data helps governments plan.

Population is the number of people living in a place, and population data helps plan schools, hospitals, roads, housing, water and energy.
The world population reached about 8 billion and is expected to be 9.7 billion by 2050, peaking around 10.3 billion in the 2080s.
Three things change a country's population: births, deaths and migration.
Birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 people in a year, and death rate is the number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.
Fertility rate is the average number of children a woman has in her lifetime.
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another, within or outside the country.
Population grew fast because better healthcare and food lowered death rates, and now growth is slowing as birth rates fall.
A population pyramid shows how many people are in each age group, split between males and females.
Many countries now face ageing populations, with more older people and fewer young workers.
The 'dependency' on working-age adults rises when there are many children or many elders.

problem.en: A town of 20,000 people has 400 births in a year. Find the birth rate.

text.en: Birth rate is births per 1,000 people.

prompt.en: What three things change a population?

points.en: Population changes by births, deaths and migration.
Birth rate and death rate are counted per 1,000 people per year.
A population pyramid shows age groups and ageing is a growing issue.
